problem:
An initial value problem has the exact solution ${y}_{\text{exact}}(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$ A numerical method is used to approximate the solution to the initial value problem, resulting in the table below, where $y$ denotes the approximate solution at each step, and ${τ}_{n}$ is the local truncation error at each step. At each step, the exact value is used to approximate the new value. 

Calculate the local truncation error at each step. Round your answers to three decimal places.

| $n$ | $x$ | $y$ | ${τ}_{n}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $0$ | $0$ | $0$ |
| $1$ | $0.25$ | $0.250$ | {{field-1}} |
| $2$ | $0.5$ | $0.483$ | {{field-2}} |
| $3$ | $0.75$ | $0.688$ | {{field-3}} |
